newsitem.title: USA: IMF sees risk of further U.S. stock market drop.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees risk of further U.S. stock market drop.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund on Wednesday saw the risk of a further big drop in stock prices in the United States and elsewhere, but suggested that it would not be enough to help trigger an economic recession.

"Recent declines in equity prices have underscored the risk of a more significant correction, especially if earnings expectations were to be downgraded or a re-emergence of inflationary pressures were to require a marked rise in interest rates," it said in its World Economic Outlook.
U.S. stock prices tumbled after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates a month ago, but they have since recouped much of those losses.
The IMF said a significant drop in stock prices could undermine confidence throughout the economy.

But whether the fall would be steep enough to contribute to a recession depends partly on the extent to which it reflects what the IMF called "a broader buildup of demand pressures." That does not seem to be the case.

"A generalized overvaluation of asset prices, leveraged by increased indebtedness, does not appear to be present in most countries with strong stock markets," the Fund said in its semi-annual look at the world economy.
In fact, it said the steep rise in U.S stock prices in recent years seemed largely justified by the fundamentals, particularly strong corporate earnings growth and low interest rates.
